title: Impact of Brainstorming-Driven Bounded Spaces Method on Developing Certain Creative Kinesthetic Abilities in Intermediate School Students
venue: International Journal of Experimental Sports Science Research
abstract: Backgroud: Traditional physical education instruction in soccer frequently relies on decontextualized command drills that detach motor execution from perceptual problem-solving. This study investigates the pedagogical impact of an 8-unit brainstorming-driven small-sided games curriculum (bounded spaces method) on developing fundamental soccer skills (ball control, slalom dribbling, and target shooting accuracy) and motor decision-making among male intermediate school students. Methods: A quasi-experimental non-equivalent control group pre-test/post-test design was conducted with 30 male second-intermediate students (aged 13–14 years) at Al-Haritha High School for Outstanding Students in Basra, Iraq, during the 2023–2024 academic year. Participants were assigned to an experimental group (n = 15, instructed via brainstorming-driven small-sided games across 4 weeks, 2 sessions/week, 45 min/session) or a control group (n = 15, instructed via conventional direct command drills). Skill batteries demonstrated high test-retest reliability (r = 0.86–0.89). Data were evaluated using paired and independent t-tests (df = 14 and df = 28), 95% confidence intervals, and effect size calculations (Cohen's d and Hedges' g). Results: While pre-test baseline measures confirmed group equivalence (p > 0.80), post-test evaluations demonstrated statistically significant superiority for the experimental group across all technical measures: ball control (mean = 8.933 vs. 7.733 points, t = 2.369, p = 0.025, Cohen's d = 0.866, 95% CI [0.163, 2.237]), dribbling agility time (mean = 12.951 s vs. 14.289 s, t = 3.229, p = 0.003, Cohen's d = -1.180, 95% CI [-2.187, -0.489]), and shooting accuracy (mean = 9.066 vs. 7.866 points, t = 2.662, p = 0.013, Cohen's d = 0.973, 95% CI [0.277, 2.123]). title: The E³P model: perception of external events and exposures in sport and exercise
venue: International Journal of Sport and Exercise Psychology
abstract: Research on perception, attention, and appraisal in sport and exercise is extensive and influential. Building on this foundation, the Integrative External Events and Exposures Perception (E³P) model is introduced as a scaffold that connects established insights and clarifies implications for research and practice. The model conceptualises perception broadly as the conversion of external events into internal information. It frames the process in three components: (a) input, encompassing sensory energies and exogenous substances that, once taken up, generate perceivable internal signals; (b) attention allocation, conceived as a depth valve that routes processing along a shallow–to–deep continuum, alongside breadth, stability, and flexibility; and (c) a four-layer sequence of meaning-making—pre-attentive perception, stimulus-driven noticing, contextual interpretation, and evaluative appraisal—that operates cumulatively and concurrently. The model outlines multiple feed-forward and feedback loops within a perception–action cycle, together with continuous interactions with proprioception, internally directed attention, and self-regulation. The model components are mapped onto five applied approaches – game-based task design, technology-mediated simulations, sensory and physiological optimisation, cognitive–attentional training, and long-term personal development – to support athlete learning and development, elite performance, and inclusive practice across diverse participants. title: Tactical decision-making following filanesia-based ecological dynamics in youth football through a multisite cluster-randomized trial
venue: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science
abstract: Background: National playing philosophies can guide youth development, but whether a culturally situated framework offers lasting benefits beyond generic game-based practice remains unclear. Aims: This study compared Filanesia-based ecological dynamics (Filanesia-ED), generic ecological dynamics (Generic-ED), and conventional coaching for retained tactical decision-making, multidomain tactical adaptation, and pressure-stratified decision accuracy. Methods: A multisite three-arm cluster-randomized trial involved 144 players nested in 12 youth football teams in Lampung and North Sumatra, Indonesia. Teams completed 16 sessions over eight weeks, with assessment at pretest, posttest, and four-week retention. Analyses included longitudinal tactical outcomes, 9,806 match-decision events, 192 fidelity observations, and 1,152 small-sided-game GPS records. Player outcomes were analyzed longitudinally, and decision events were examined using generalized estimating equations. Findings were interpreted in the context of 12 randomized teams. Result: The longitudinal model showed a condition-by-time interaction, Wald χ²(4) = 363.83, p < .001. At posttest, the adjusted Filanesia-ED advantage was 12.59 points versus conventional coaching (95% CI [8.51, 16.67]) and 6.32 points versus Generic-ED (95% CI [2.25, 10.39]); corresponding retention differences were 11.33 and 6.75 points. In the event-level analysis, Filanesia-ED had higher odds of a correct decision under high opponent pressure than conventional coaching, OR = 1.74, 95% CI [1.33, 2.27], p < .001. Conclusion: Filanesia-ED was associated with higher posttest and retained tactical decision-making scores than either comparison. title: “Expertise guides where attention lies”: exploring climbers’ attentional focus during route preview using eye-tracking and verbal reports
venue: International Journal of Sport and Exercise Psychology
abstract: Route preview, the visual inspection of climbing movements prior to motor execution, has attracted scientific interest over the past decades. From a sport psychology perspective, elucidating factors underlying differences in attentional focus during route preview appears promising for advancing understanding of how expertise shapes attentional processes in climbing and other relatively closed sporting contexts. This study examined attentional focus during route preview across climbers of varying skill levels by analysing gaze behaviour using portable eye-tracking. Twenty-five intermediate, advanced, and elite climbers previewed and attempted an Olympic boulder problem. Data collection included gaze behaviour during route preview alongside concurrent think-aloud and retrospective verbal reports, as well as climbing performance metrics. Besides lower climbing performance, intermediate climbers showed longer preview and total absolute fixation durations at holds than advanced and elite climbers. Despite similar overall relative fixations, the spatial distribution of these fixations differed between the groups; advanced and elite climbers displayed a more homogeneous pattern with lower variability, allocating a greater proportion of fixations to the middle and final sections of the boulder, whereas intermediate climbers focused more on the starting section. Verbal reports similarly revealed skill-level differences in attentional distribution and factors shaping attentional focus toward task-relevant holds. Findings suggest that attentional focus during route preview reflects an interplay among cognitive processing of movement demands, task difficulty relative to skill level, and perceived task-relevant priorities. title: Impact of perceived social risk on the tendency toward sports gambling addiction among Chinese recreational sports club members: verifying the mediating effect of sports values
abstract: Introduction This study examines the associations between perceived social risk and the tendency toward sports gambling addiction among recreational sports club members in China, with particular attention to the potential indirect role of sports values. Drawing on general strain theory and psychosocial value frameworks, perceived social risk is conceptualized as a multidimensional perception of economic, interpersonal, psychological, and physical pressures in everyday social and recreational contexts, while the COVID-19 period is treated as contextual background rather than as part of the construct itself. Methods Using data from 362 recreational sports participants with previous sports lottery purchasing experience, the study employed confirmatory factor analysis, multiple regression, and bootstrap mediation analysis. Results Economic, psychological, and interpersonal risks were positively associated with gambling tendency, whereas physical risk was not significant. In the parallel multiple-mediator models, the total indirect effect through the five sports-value dimensions was significant for economic, interpersonal, and psychological risk, but not for physical risk. Among the 20 specific indirect effects, only the pathway from interpersonal risk through character values to gambling tendency had a 95% bootstrap confidence interval that excluded zero. Discussion The findings provide exploratory evidence concerning the relationships among perceived social risk, sports values, and gambling tendency in this sample, while highlighting the need for longitudinal and cross-cultural research with more representative samples.

title: Tactical behaviour in elite U-12 boys’ tennis: an observational mixed methods case study of the Open Super 12 Auray tournament
abstract: Evidence on tactical behaviour in elite U-12 tennis remains limited, particularly regarding how the serve interacts with rally development and point outcome. This observational mixed methods case study used a quantitatively driven qual → QUAN → qual analytical sequence to characterise the tactical profile of elite international U-12 boys competing at the 2023 Open Super 12 Auray tournament. Spontaneous match behaviours were systematically observed, transformed into coded categorical data using the OBSTENNIS-JUNIOR-S23 observational instrument, analysed quantitatively, and subsequently interpreted within their competitive and developmental context. A total of 557 points from seven matches involving eight players were analysed. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, Cramér’s V, adjusted standardised residuals, and conditional winning probabilities were calculated. Point outcome was relatively balanced between server (46.7%) and receiver (53.3%). After excluding double faults, the server won 53.7% of first-serve points and 43.3% of second-serve points. Body serves predominated overall (59.4%) and were especially frequent on second serves (91.0%). Short rallies accounted for 53.1% of points, although rally length was not associated with point outcome. Unforced errors were the main route to point resolution. The integrated observational mixed methods approach enabled the construction of a contextualised tactical profile of elite U-12 boys’ tennis. These findings indicate that, in this competitive case, the serve did not provide a clear overall tactical advantage and support training approaches that combine serve-placement variability, serve–return–third-shot sequences, rally consistency, and error management.

title: Blocked vs. randomized practice shapes coordination across adaptation, retention, and transfer following perturbation-based balance training in young adults
venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
abstract: Perturbation-based balance training (PBT) improves reactive balance control, but it remains unclear whether increased practice variability, particularly the contextual interference effect (CIE), enhances retention and transfer. This study investigated whether blocked vs. randomized PBT schedules differently influence adaptation, retention, transfer, and coordination patterns. Thirty-two healthy young adults completed a single-session PBT with repeated trip perturbations under either a blocked or randomized schedule. Retention and intra-task transfer were evaluated using trained and untrained trip perturbations, and inter-task transfer was tested with a simulated forward fall. Dynamic stability performance was assessed using the margin of stability (MoS), and whole-body kinematic synergies (kSYNs) were extracted via principal component analysis to investigate coordinative changes. No significant improvements in MoS were observed during practice, and contrary to expectations derived from the CIE, randomized practice did not show superior retention, or transfer compared to blocked practice at the performance level. kSYNs revealed training-related adaptations and group differences, including changes in knee flexion contribution and stepping coordination. However, limited shared kSYNs between perturbed walking and simulated forward falls indicate strong task specificity. Together, these findings suggest that practice schedule influenced coordination patterns but did not translate into superior stability outcomes in young adults following single-session PBT.

title: Cardiovascular responses of hypertensive older women after isometric handgrip exercise performed with an inflatable ball: a randomized, controlled crossover clinical trial
venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
abstract: Background Isometric handgrip exercise (IHG) has been proposed as a non-pharmacological strategy for the management of blood pressure (BP) in hypertensive individuals. However, the effects of IHG on post-exercise hypotension (PEH), defined as an immediate reduction in blood pressure following exercise, remain poorly understood, particularly in trained hypertensive older women. Objective This study aimed to investigate the BP and cardiac autonomic modulation (CAM) responses of trained hypertensive older women post IHG performed with an inflatable ball. Methods This randomized, controlled crossover clinical trial included 12 trained hypertensive older women (≥ 60 years) under stable antihypertensive medication. Participants completed two experimental conditions: IHG performed at 30% of maximal voluntary isometric contraction (MVIC) and a sham condition at 3% MVIC. Each condition consisted of eight 1-minute contractions interspersed with 1-minute rest intervals. Blood pressure (BP) and heart rate variability (HRV) were assessed pre-condition and at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min post-conditions. Results No significant interaction effects were observed for systolic BP, diastolic BP, mean BP, or HRV indices ( p > 0.05). Conclusion A single session of IHG performed using an inflatable ball (8 × 1-minute contractions interspersed with 1-minute rest intervals) did not alter post-exercise BP or CAM responses in trained hypertensive older women with well-controlled resting BP.

title: How to build a high-impact traditional sports culture brand in universities: an empirical study based on the 23-year dragon boat program at Liaocheng University, China
venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
abstract: Amidst the backdrop of national cultural advancement and the deepening fusion of sports and education, establishing traditional sports brands in universities plays a crucial role in preserving Chinese heritage, enhancing university competitiveness, and fostering students' comprehensive growth. This paper examines the 23-year evolution (2002–2025) of Dragon Boat Team of Liaocheng University (LCU-DBT). In the literature review, case analysis, field interviews and proportional conversion analysis, the fundamental components, and cooperative mechanisms of building university dragon boat sport (DBS) brands are investigated. Our results show that, using the advantages and cultural heritage of the Grand Canal in the “Water City in Northern China (WCNC)”, Liaocheng University (LCU) has developed a four-dimensional collaborative brand with top level assurance, core support, promotion and communication, and external outreach. LCU integrates ideological development, institutional innovation, financial support, talent cultivation, scientific training, media promotion, and international exchange to foster competitive strength and cultural brand growth. LCU's university-sports brand-building serves as an illustrative reference for advancing traditional sports within higher-education institutions. However, the brand construction still suffers from vague positioning, insufficient cultural exploration, inadequate resource support, and discontinuous talent echelons. Accordingly, our study proposes five-dimensional integrated development model for university intangible cultural heritage sports which includes popularization infrastructure, diversification of commercial activities, systematic cultural communication, talent feedback, and digital-based archiving and dissemination. title: Bioinspired trajectory tracking control of an underactuated robotic fish using prescribed-time and prescribed-performance control.
abstract: Fish swimming couples rhythmic body deformation, distributed coordination, and environmental interaction to produce propulsion and maneuvering. This study asks how these principles can inspire trajectory regulation for an underactuated robotic fish. A three-joint body-caudal model driven by a coupled central pattern generator is combined with prescribed-performance guidance, a filtered reduced-order observer, and a bounded prescribed-time regulator. Lateral control is treated as virtual guidance and realized through coordinated heading and body-caudal motion rather than an independently actuated sway force. A practical prescribed-time boundedness result accounts for observer, model, sampling, and actuator effects. Validation combines numerical simulation, an independent physics-based UE5 environment, and outdoor lake experiments. The two available lake runs achieve position RMSEs of 0.3768 m and 0.2600 m for straight and circular trajectories, respectively. The results show that the virtual lateral-guidance channel substantially improves spatial tracking and that the bioinspired locomotion structure can be carried from modeling to physical deployment.

title: "Beyond practice hours"- A systematic review of elite football development pathways.
venue: Frontiers in sports and active living
abstract: This systematic review synthesised research on the developmental activities of elite male football players and evaluated what existing evidence reveals about variation in developmental pathways across populations and contexts. Guided by the Developmental Model of Sport Participation, a framework synthesis was employed to integrate predominantly quantitative data within a qualitative, context-sensitive approach. Eighteen peer-reviewed studies were included following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, examining engagement in domain-specific activities (structured training, competition and informal play) and non-domain-specific activities (other sports). Early exposure to football was consistent across the reviewed studies, with differentiation towards elite performance emerging during adolescence through increased structured, coach-led practice. Evidence supporting early diversification was inconsistent, while engagement in informal play varied considerably across populations. Although developmental activity patterns differed between populations, the primary studies rarely measured the socio-cultural, institutional or environmental conditions potentially associated with these differences. The review extends existing knowledge by distinguishing between evidence describing what elite players did during development and evidence explaining why particular developmental pathways emerged. The findings suggest that expertise development may reflect a dynamic interaction between structured training and socio-cultural environments, supporting a context-dependent understanding of football expertise. Future research should combine developmental activity histories with direct measurements of contextual factors to better explain how different pathways to elite football emerge. PROSPERO identifier
